newsitem.title: UK: Mandela tells world not to fear his retirement.
newsitem.headline: Mandela tells world not to fear his retirement.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday told the world not to fear his retirement, saying his successors were at least as capable as he was.

"I am a member of a robust team of leaders and a very capital collective, some of whom have abilities and powers to think far greater than I could imagine for myself," Mandela told a BBC interviewer who asked how South Africa would ever replace him.
"I can assure the entire world that they have nothing to worry about," Mandela added.
The South African president, who is on a four-day visit to Britain with his companion Grace Machel, has already handed over much of his work to his deputy Thabo Mbeki.
"The real ruler of South Africa, the de facto ruler of South Africa, is Thabo Mbeki...I am shifting everything to him and he is doing remarkably well," Mandela said.
Mandela and Machel, the widow of former Mozambican president Samora Machel, arrived in London earlier on Tuesday. Machel is here to receive an honorary degree from a British university.
The couple had tea with Queen Elizabeth during the afternoon and Mandela was due to receive the freedom of the city of Oxford on Friday.
He was also due to deliver a lecture to the Centre for Islamic Studies, attend a dinner with Prince Charles and meet Britain's new prime minister, Tony Blair.

As he strolled across the tarmac at Heathrow airport, wearing his trademark patterned shirt and slacks, the 78-year-old president said he had only flown to Britain to accompany Machel to her graduation ceremony.
"I am accompanying Mrs Machel," he told reporters. "As you know she is receiving an honorary degree at the University of Essex and I come here as her companion."
Machel is an international ambassador for children's rights, and has accompanied Mandela on a number of trips.
Arriving at their London hotel, the couple were asked by reporters if they had plans to marry.
The couple looked at each other and smiled before Mandela, with Machel's head briefly resting on his shoulder, said: "Those are questions one doesn't discuss in public."

Mandela's meeting with Blair will be his first with Britain's Labour government, elected in May, which had close links with the anti-apartheid movement during Mandela's imprisonment and South Africa's international isolation.
The South African government is in mid-winter recess and the president is expected to travel on to Thailand and Indonesia.
